findings.summary: Round four's case-sensitive grep is genuinely gone, but the wording that replaced it makes the same class of claim one more time -- the list lives on the M5.6e backlog row, which names each site and line -- and the M5.6e row's enumeration is not each site: it names only SPEC.md 5/11/18/377 and roadmap.md's M5 row, while backlog.md:18, twenty-eight lines above M5.6e in the same file, still asserts closure at an even earlier task.
findings.failure_scenario: backlog.md:18 reads It owns the commit forwarding M4 deferred, so a multi-pod deployment is incorrect until M5.4 lands -- i.e. correct once M5.4 lands. M5.4 is RemoteSequencer, an earlier task than the M5.6/M5.6b this commit spends five rounds denying closure for. It is untouched by this diff and appears in no round's finding: round three grepped over docs/internal/product/ and reported only SPEC.md:5,11,18,377 and roadmap.md:14, and the M5.6e row copied exactly that five-item list. Concretely: an agent at M5.20, told by this javadoc that M5.6e names each site and line, corrects those five and leaves the authoritative task list's own current-milestone header saying the hole shuts at M5.4 -- so backlog.md then carries both answers about the same hole in one file. Minor because no source or backlog row now says M5.6b closes it; the defect is that a fourth completeness claim in this commit is again not complete.

findings.summary: Round four's R2 is fixed -- the bare (M2.1) is gone from both rows -- but the replacement wording overshoots in the other direction: both rows now call the SequencerTransport gap unowned, which the M5.6e row in the same table contradicts in the same diff.
findings.failure_scenario: backlog.md:40 reads it needs a production SequencerTransport and a production main(), both unowned and both recorded on M5.6e, and backlog.md:43 reads both gaps are unowned and recorded on M5.6e. backlog.md:46 is M5.6e | A production SequencerTransport ... | FR-11 | todo, owned by M8, and its own text says it is recorded here so it stops being unowned. So the transport half of both unowned is false as of this commit: M5.6e owns it and names M8. Only the main() half is genuinely unowned. Concretely: an agent reads M5.6 or M5.6b, takes the SequencerTransport is unowned at face value, and either files a second row duplicating M5.6e or reports to a person that nothing owns the production transport when M8 does -- the mirror image of the earlier finding that (M2.1) overstated ownership.

findings.summary: The standing-authority header now states both that the grant was WIDENED on 2026-09-09 to any round past the cap and, four lines later, that This is a narrowing of the mechanism, not a widening -- so the one paragraph a reader consults to decide whether a fifth-round signature was inside the grant gives both answers.
findings.failure_scenario: The pre-existing narrowing sentence meant narrowing relative to the archived REVIEW_ROUND_BUDGET escape hatch, but the widening text was spliced in ahead of it and now supplies the immediate antecedent, so the sentence reads as denying the sentence before it. This commit's own fifth-round line is signed On the standing M5 authority as widened, so a person auditing whether that signature was earned -- the single stated purpose of this file -- is handed a header that says the grant both was and was not widened. Minor because the round-five line names its conditions explicitly and all three are checkable against review/verdicts/M5.6b/.
